text:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - elevated KV cache paging across multiple Dedicated pools in us-west-2, memory pressure + NCCL stalls detected on tp shards. Auto-escalation to oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Looking. Any early customer impact?

mira: Seeing sustained swap/paging on nvme for kv-store processes. Continuous-batching token accumulation spiked after 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC deploy (runtime 2.4.1 -> 2.4.2). Memory climbed from ~35% to 92% in some shards.

alex: Also catching NCCL ERROR: unhandled stall on tp-device-3 -> logs: `ncclNetGdr_regMr failed` and `tensor-split imbalance: shard 7 45% utilization, shard 3 2%` — looks like uneven KV partitioning after the sharding tweak in 2.4.2.

samir: Confirmed correlation with the new continuous_batching heuristics: config `continuous_batch_window_ms` lowered from 8 -> 2 and `max_continuous_tokens` raised 128 -> 512 in the same rollout. That increased in-flight KV entries and memory blowups.

oncall-sre: Immediate mitigation options?

mira: Two prongs: 1) hotfix to restore previous batching defaults (8ms / 128 tokens) and throttle continuous batching; 2) emergency rebalance of KV shards to even partitions to stop hot-spotting and reduce NCCL cross-device traffic.

samir: I can push the hotfix patch to runtime config. Plan: edit configmap `runtime-inference` in prod-usw2 -> set `continuous_batch_window_ms: 8` and `max_continuous_tokens: 128`, and disable tensor-parallel dynamic split for the time being.

ops-bot: CI/CD deploy started for runtime-config-hotfix-20260315 by samir. Rolling update to inference-runtime pods in prod-usw2 with maintenance windows off.

alex: Pushing the config now. Patch: ```yaml
# runtime config patch
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  continuous_batch_window_ms: 8
  max_continuous_tokens: 128
tensor_parallel:
  dynamic_split: false
```

ops-bot: Rollout progress: 3/8 nodes updated. Healthchecks passing on updated pods.

mira: Early telemetry: memory pressure dipping on updated hosts, network NCCL retransmit counts falling ~15% on updated nodes. But two shards still showing >70% memory (shard-7, shard-11).

alex: I see an nccl log tail on shard-7: ```
[NCCL][ERROR] Timeout waiting for remote op
Device 3 -> Device 7: flow stall
KVShardBalancer: failed handshake: partition mismatch
```

oncall-sre: For the overloaded shards, recommend immediate local eviction + reduce shard replica weight to move new allocations away. Can we trigger a manual rebalance?

mira: Yes. I can run the KV shard rebalance with `kv-shard-balancer --dry-run` first then execute. Plan: move ~20% of prefixes off shard-7 onto shard-3/shard-4 which are underutilized.

samir: Manual rebalance started (non-disruptive handoff mode). Command: `kv-shard-balancer --target shard-7 --drain 20 --mode handoff`

incident-bot: Note: This operation will temporarily increase inter-shard traffic and may produce short-lived latency spikes.

kate: I'll open a customer-impact thread. Which tenants are affected?

mira: Affected tenants list from logs: ["shoply-prod", "clx-ads", "edu-align"]. Latency spike 99p tokens increased from 120ms -> 2.4s for those tenants between 02:11-02:42 UTC. Errors: ~0.4% 5xx increase.

oncall-sre: Notify account teams. kate, pinging you: @kate please escalate to account leads, include mitigation plan and ETA for stabilization (~30-45m).

kate: On it. Message drafted and sent to account ops. Asked for customer-facing note with ETA.

ops-bot: Rebalance step 1/5 complete. Moved 12% of prefixes off shard-7 -> shard-3. No errors.

mira: Post-move metrics: shard-7 memory down 9%, overall NCCL stalls reduced. However, shard-11 still showing high swap due to a large hot prefix set (long prefix chains). Need to evict stale KV entries for that prefix set.

samir: I can force-run prefix garbage collection on shard-11: `kv-gc --shard shard-11 --age-threshold 48h --force`

alex: Running gc now. Watch for spike in disk I/O.

incident-bot: GC job started on shard-11 (job id: gc-20260315-01). Expected duration ~6m.

mira: GC complete. Freed ~42GB on shard-11. Swap down to normal. NCCL retransmit count normalized.

ops-bot: Runtime-config-hotfix rollout complete: 8/8 nodes updated. Health: OK.

oncall-sre: Good. Telemetry shows 99p latency for affected tenants back to <200ms, 5xx rate back to baseline. No further NCCL errors in the last 4m.

kate: Customer update: sent note at 03:02 UTC - describing root-cause (batching defaults + sharder mismatch), actions taken (hotfix, rebalance, GC), and current status (stabilized).

alex: Leaving a log snippet for postmortem: `runtime 2.4.2` introduced two coupled changes: batching window reduction + sharder heuristics tweak. The combination increased KV live set and created uneven partitioning under certain traffic skew -> led to memory exhaustion on some shards and NCCL stalls between TP peers.

mira: Next steps: 1) revert sharder heuristic until we have better provable balance properties; 2) add surge-protection limit for continuous-batching in prod (hard cap on in-flight kv entries per model); 3) add early warning alert on per-shard memory delta > 20%/5m.

oncall-sre: Agreed. I'll open JIRA for the sharder revert + tests. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

samir: I'll follow up with a canary plan for any future batching heuristic changes (gradual ramp + per-shard mem guardrails).

kate: Handoff to next oncall: @kate handing to @alex for monitoring and follow-up. Alex, can you keep an eye until 08:00 UTC?

alex: Acknowledged. I'll run a 4h watch and collect traces.

oncall-sre: Incident state -> mitigated. We'll publish a short postmortem after deeper analysis. Thanks team :green_heart: 

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 03:12 UTC. Postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGINF-3129
